title: Adaptive mid-cycle quota smoothing for prepaid reserved customers
creator: Asha R. Patel
description:
Background:
Customers on Reserved capacity buy committed token/throughput buckets for a month but real usage can vary wildly. Today we reset buckets at month boundary (and support some prorated transfers for migrations). This produces two operational issues for high-variance tenants: 1) wasted prepaid capacity when usage is well below commitment for long stretches, and 2) sudden throttling when a tenant leans into bursty traffic mid-cycle with no soft cushion.

Goal:
Design and ship an adaptive mid-cycle smoothing mechanism that: (a) grants a temporary soft-credit buffer to tenants that are underutilizing their reserved allocation earlier in the cycle, (b) decays unused soft-credit gradually so we don't accumulate unbounded credit, (c) reclaims soft-credit predictably under high contention and (d) exposes transparent accounting and billing signals so finance and customers can reconcile usage.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Compute a per-tenant running utilization factor U(t) over a sliding window (configurable, default 7 days) weighted toward recent usage.
- If U(t) < low_util_threshold (default 0.55) we create a temporary soft-credit S = floor((1 - U(t)) * reserved_monthly_quota * alpha) where alpha is a tunable aggressiveness parameter (default 0.25).
- Soft-credit is consumed before overage tokens but is subject to a decay schedule: S(t+1) = S(t) * decay_beta per day (default decay_beta=0.9).
- Reclamation policy: under cluster-wide capacity pressure or when tenant spikes > spike_protect_limit (configurable) we mark soft-credit as reclaimable and reduce S by reclaim_fraction (default 0.5) to preserve tail latency for best-effort tenants.
- Accounting: every soft-credit grant and decay event emits an immutable ledger entry with reason, amount, timestamp, and causal window id. These are exported to billing pipelines and the console.

API / data model changes:
- new fields on tenant_quota object: soft_credit_current (int tokens), soft_credit_history_id (string), soft_credit_state (ACTIVE|RECLAIMABLE|EXPIRED).
- admin endpoints: POST /admin/tenants/{id}/soft-credit/adjust, GET /admin/tenants/{id}/soft-credit/history
- telemetry: metric rwi.quota.soft_credit.granted, rwi.quota.soft_credit.reclaimed, rwi.quota.soft_credit.decayed (tagged by tenant, pool, and window_id)

Why this vs. allowing intra-month carry-forward or full banking?
- Full carry-forward complicates billing reconciliation and materially impacts capacity planning for Reserved pools. Soft credits are ephemeral, capped, and decay to avoid long-term liability while improving customer experience.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow: system grants soft-credit for a simulated tenant with low week-long utilization and lets that credit be consumed during a synthetic burst; credits decay and are reclaimed under simulated pressure.
- Telemetry: grant/reclaim/decay metrics appear in Datadog with tenant tags and aggregate SLO (<5s latency for admin endpoints).
- Billing: exported ledger rows are consumable by finance ETL and appear on the reconciliation QA playground (link in comments).
- Console: tenant usage page shows current soft_credit and clear explanation of its transient nature.
- Performance: quota check path latency increase < 1ms p50 on critical path in canary cluster.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): enable for 5 low-risk tenant accounts (QA + two customers that opted in). Monitor rwi.quota.soft_credit.* and cost delta.
- Phase 2 (gradual): enable for all Reserved accounts in region us-west-2 with alpha=0.15.
- Phase 3: GA with alpha=0.25 and console flag.

Open design questions:
- Optimal defaults for alpha and decay_beta (we'll run an offline sweep using 12 months of tenancy traces).
- Edge cases for cross-tenant pooled reserved capacity: should soft-credit be allowed to spill across multiple reservations? (initial stance: no).
- Legal/billing labeling: how to present soft-credit on invoices (prepaid adjustment line vs informational).
comments: 2026-02-19 - Asha: Initial proposal posted. Need input from finance on ledger schema — @Marisol to advise.
2026-02-22 - Marisol (Finance): Ledger row ok but we need an explicit liability bucket and a max lifetime of 21 days for any soft credits before forced expiration.

2026-02-26 - Liam: Implemented prototype in rwi-quota-service, added grant/decay loop and basic metrics (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rwi/quota/pull/1427). Early perf looks good on dev cluster.
2026-03-03 - Design review (SRE): Added reclamation hook for cluster pressure; SRE suggests reducing reclaim_fraction to 0.33 to avoid oscillation. Will test both values in chaos runs.
2026-03-08 - PM feedback (Noah): Console UX needs copy that clearly states 'soft credits are temporary and do not change your billed commitment'. Noah opened PM task PM-411 for copy and billing FAQ.

2026-03-12 - QA: Wrote integration tests covering grant -> consume -> decay -> forced reclaim. Found race where simultaneous grant and reclaim could produce negative soft_credit; added atomic compare-and-swap on tenant state.
